method: Web searches per company: '<company> IPO review analysis', '<company> IPO risk factors prospectus', '<company> IPO anchor investors', '<company> IPO GMP subscription day'; plus a direct check of cached investorgain.com source JSON to resolve a promoter-holding data discrepancy shared by four issues.

Lumino Industries Limited.summary: A quality domestic-mutual-fund anchor book and a cheap peer multiple are real positives, but the balance sheet carries more stress than the ratios show: rising debt, negative FY25 operating cash flow, and stretched receivables.

items.text: Borrowings had risen to ₹1,856.78 Cr as of 31 Jul 2026, with negative operating cash flow in FY25 and trade receivables at 43.84% of FY26 revenue; debtor days stand at 145 and net working capital is 35.11% of FY26 revenue.
Aluminium is 83.25% of raw-material cost, leaving margins exposed to commodity swings.

Anchor book of ₹207 Cr drew 30 institutions, 71.59% from domestic mutual funds (HDFC, Kotak, Motilal Oswal, Bandhan, Edelweiss, JM Financial, Bank of India) plus Abakkus Growth Fund (Sunil Singhania) — a genuinely long-only book, though with zero FPI participation.

Revenue is concentrated with government entities/SEBs as major customers; prospectus discloses ongoing litigation involving the company, promoters and directors, none flagged as material as of the RHP date.
Most brokerages (Sushil Finance, SBI Securities, Ventura, Adroit) rate it Subscribe, citing valuation cheaper than KEC International (19.8x) and Kalpataru Projects (22.1x) FY26 P/E.

Lumino Industries Limited.adjustment_reason: Agree with the computed CONSIDER, not APPLY. The cheap relative multiple and strong domestic-MF anchor book are genuine positives, but rising leverage and negative FY25 operating cash flow are exactly what a pure P/E/GMP score can't see, and argue against a higher-conviction call.

Kwick Forensic Solutions Limited.summary: Strong revenue growth and a cheap headline P/E sit on a small, tender-dependent, geographically concentrated business anchored only by second-tier alternative-investment funds with no marquee long-only name.

items.text: Top 10 customers are 77.64% of revenue; government dependence is 55.22%; Gujarat and Bihar alone account for ~38.41% of revenue.
Company incurred over ₹15 lakh in penalties for delayed EPF, GST, TDS and advance-tax filings in recent years.

Anchor book raised only ₹14.43 Cr from 10 institutions led by Bharat Venture Opportunities Fund (18.76%) plus smaller AIFs (Finavenue, CP Capital, Tiger Strategies) — no mutual fund, insurer, or pension fund participated.
Revenue grew from ₹65.08 Cr (FY25) to ₹105.80 Cr (FY26) and profit from ₹8.56 Cr to ₹13.51 Cr.
No independent coverage found of related-party transactions or specific litigation beyond generic risk-factor boilerplate — a genuine coverage gap for this SME issue, not filled with speculation.

Kwick Forensic Solutions Limited.adjustment_reason: I would push toward AVOID / high-caution rather than the computed CONSIDER. Customer and geographic concentration, compliance penalties, and an anchor book with zero institutional heavyweight participation outweigh the growth numbers, especially given the ₹1.44 lakh minimum lot makes this a large, illiquid, hard-to-exit single bet.

Priority Jewels Limited.summary: The computed score's most bearish input — a 100% promoter exit — is very likely a data artifact, not a real event; the actual structural concerns are customer concentration and a tight working-capital cycle.

items.text: DATA CORRECTION: the pipeline's promoter_post=0.00% is very likely an unfilled placeholder in the source (investorgain.com), not a real full exit. This issue has 0% OFS (100% fresh issue) — a genuine full promoter exit is mechanically impossible through a fresh-issue-only structure. Back-of-envelope math from disclosed pre-issue holding (1.26 crore shares, 93.85%) against the post-issue share base implies promoters retain roughly 70%, not 0%. Independent sources (Bajaj Broking, Chittorgarh) confirm zero OFS and do not report any promoter exit.
items.source: cached investorgain.com JSON + Bajaj Broking, Chittorgarh

items.text: Top 10 customers are 53.2% of Q1 FY27 revenue — meaningful concentration for a jewellery retailer.
Working capital cycle is 148-164 days with ₹96.75 Cr secured borrowings as of June 2026; raw materials are 92.5% of FY26 costs, making margins gold-price sensitive.
DRHP discloses ongoing related-party transactions with no assurance that terms are equivalent to arm's-length.
Anchor book raised only ₹27.45 Cr — modest size for a ₹91.5 Cr issue.
One broker (via Equentis) called the issue 'fully priced' at 20.5x FY26 P/E but still rated it 'Subscribe for Long Term'.

Priority Jewels Limited.adjustment_reason: Agree with the computed CONSIDER, but for different reasons than the tool states. Ignore the 'full promoter exit' evidence line — it is almost certainly a source data placeholder rather than a real 0% holding. The real caution points are customer concentration and a stretched working-capital cycle typical of a jewellery trader.

Esds Software Solution Limited.summary: A genuinely long-only anchor book and strong revenue/profit growth partly justify the rich multiple, but declining return on equity, heavily pledged current assets, and an unresolved equity litigation claim are exactly what the valuation multiple alone can't show.

items.text: Anchor book was ₹216 Cr, with domestic mutual funds (Motilal Oswal, Bandhan, Quant, ITI, JM Financial, Samco) taking 82% of the allocation — a genuinely long-only quality book.
A former employee (Rajeev Papneja) claims entitlement to 1% equity or ₹184.8 million in compensation, per prospectus disclosure.
96.72% of current assets were hypothecated/pledged to lenders as of 31 March 2026, and the prospectus warns lenders could sell pledged shares.
FY26 revenue grew 28% and PAT grew 117% YoY (₹120.8 Cr vs ₹55.6 Cr).
RoNW of 13.7%, down from 22.9%, looks weak relative to the 41.6x post-issue multiple being paid; one reviewer explicitly recommended 'watchlist' over subscribe.

Esds Software Solution Limited.adjustment_reason: Agree with the computed NEUTRAL. Anchor quality and growth are real, but declining RoNW, heavily pledged current assets, and a live equity claim offset them enough to avoid a conviction call either way.

Paluck Technologies Limited.summary: A cheap headline P/E and unusually early institutional demand are real, but they sit on top of a one-year profit spike that even a bullish tracker flags as needing scrutiny, plus a documentation irregularity in the offer papers.

items.text: Business is diversified engineering/infra services: automobile and telecom-tower engineering (7,500+ sites serviced), plus logistics and equipment rental (92 transit mixers, 13 concrete pumps, 23 trucks); evolved from a diesel-generator servicing business.
FY25 net profit jumped from ₹3.43 Cr to ₹9.63 Cr — IPO Watch itself flags this 'sudden profit surge' as needing scrutiny, and notes post-IPO NAV data is garbled in the offer documents.

QIB book showed 10.49x demand unusually early (Day 1, 28 Aug) for an SME issue, per Chittorgarh/IPO Guru — real early conviction, but cannot be distinguished from SME-typical operator-driven bidding using public sources alone.
Anchor book raised only ₹9.39 Cr with no disclosed anchor names — thin and unnamed, typical for small SME issues, and doesn't confirm serious long-only participation.
IPO Watch rates it 'Subscribe' for well-informed investors on a medium-to-long-term view, citing 6.62x FY26-annualized P/E.
No independent source discussed related-party transactions, litigation, or pledged promoter shares — a genuine coverage gap, not filled with speculation.

Paluck Technologies Limited.adjustment_reason: I would soften the computed APPLY toward 'apply cautiously.' The profit surge that even IPO Watch calls out as unexplained, and the NAV documentation issue, are real diligence flags the P/E-and-subscription-driven score cannot see.

Complete Sports And Management India Lim.summary: Reasonable profitability ratios mask very weak market reception, and the 100% promoter-exit figure driving the bearish qualitative score is very likely a data artifact rather than a confirmed event.

items.text: DATA CORRECTION: promoter_post=0.00% is very likely an unfilled placeholder in the source (investorgain.com) rather than a real event — this issue also has 0% OFS (100% fresh issue), the same pattern seen on Priority Jewels, Purple Style Labs, and Rays of Belief. No independent source corroborates a full promoter exit; a genuine full exit is not mechanically possible through a fresh-issue-only structure without an undisclosed separate share transfer.

Business sources, trades, and distributes amusement/leisure equipment, and is forward-integrating into operating family entertainment centres and mall gaming zones (including a new 'Duckpin' centre in Mumbai).
PAT margin 15.81%, ROE 53.55%, ROCE 47.97%, manageable debt (₹8.99 Cr); post-issue P/E ~15.27x is not obviously cheap for an SME.
Chanakya Nipothi rates it 4/5 'Apply' but explicitly conditions this on GMP/subscription staying healthy — they are not: GMP is flat at 0% and subscription is only 0.12-0.13x through day 2.
No source discussed related-party transactions, litigation, or customer/supplier concentration — thin coverage typical of, and itself a risk for, SME issues.

Complete Sports And Management India Lim.adjustment_reason: Agree with the computed NEUTRAL, but discount the 'full promoter exit' evidence line as a likely data artifact. The genuine warning sign here is zero grey-market interest combined with sub-1x subscription through day 2 — a classic weak-listing setup that argues for caution regardless of the promoter-holding number.

Purple Style Labs Limited.summary: This is Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, a loss-making luxury/designer fashion e-commerce platform whose losses widened, not narrowed, year over year, and which carries a working-capital deficit — a strong anchor book is the only real counterweight.

items.text: Business is Pernia's Pop-Up Shop (PPUS), an omnichannel luxury/designer fashion platform with 1,100+ designer brands.

PAT fell 51% YoY (FY25 to FY26) even as revenue rose 15% — losses are widening, not merely persisting, despite the margin figures (-38.45% vs -51.16%) reading as improvement in isolation. Current liabilities exceed current assets by ₹255.12 Cr.
Top 10 designer brands are 30.24% of platform GMV in FY26, and brand agreements are non-exclusive, creating concentration and defection risk; no listed peer exists, so pricing is unanchored.

Anchor book raised ₹306 Cr from ICICI Prudential MF, Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance, ITI MF, Jupiter India Fund, plus BofA Securities and Morgan Stanley Asia; domestic MFs took 32.68% of the anchor allocation — a genuinely credible book.

DATA NOTE: promoter_post=0.00% follows the same pattern seen on Priority Jewels, Complete Sports, and Rays of Belief (0% OFS, likely unfilled source placeholder), though promoter_pre here is already low (26.34%) after prior VC dilution, so a further large reduction is plausible even if not literally to zero.

Purple Style Labs Limited.adjustment_reason: Agree with AVOID, and if anything the computed confidence (0.77) understates the case: the fresh PAT decline (-51% YoY, not just a persistently thin margin) and the working-capital deficit are real deterioration, not stability, in a discretionary luxury category. The strong anchor names signal institutional appetite for the story, not a profitability turnaround.

Phychem Technologies Limited.summary: Improving profitability and a diversified customer base are real positives largely invisible in the raw ratios, but a meaningful P/E discrepancy against an independent source and a total absence of named anchor investors are genuine gaps.

items.text: Business manufactures rotational-molding (roto-molding) polyethylene compounds for hollow plastic products — a niche industrial-chemicals supplier, not pharma.
Customer base includes roughly 265 domestic and 24 global customers across ~21 export countries; exports are 23.32% of FY26 revenue, somewhat mitigating concentration risk.
items.source: search synthesis, unattributed secondary source - treat as indicative only

items.text: FY25 PAT grew 68% with improving EBITDA and lower borrowings; however, one independent source pegs post-issue P/E at 19.42x versus the 13.5x in our computed figures - a real discrepancy worth flagging.
No named anchor investors could be found in any source - only that an anchor tranche of 7.68 lakh shares exists structurally. Explicitly no credible finding on anchor quality.
GMP is inconsistent across trackers: ₹3 (~5.6%) on some, ₹0 on another - thin and contradictory, consistent with normal SME pre-listing noise rather than a genuine signal.

Phychem Technologies Limited.adjustment_reason: Keep the computed NEUTRAL but lean slightly cautious given the unresolved valuation discrepancy (13.5x vs 19.42x) - re-verify the post-issue P/E before the closing-day call. Promoter dilution to 72.56% and lack of anchor disclosure are typical SME opacity, not disqualifying on their own.

Deepa Jewellers Limited.summary: Strong ROE/ROCE and revenue growth are real, but they say nothing about the gold-price and working-capital exposure inherent to jewellery trading, or the fact that nearly half the issue proceeds go to selling shareholders rather than the company.

items.text: Business is a jewellery wholesaler/trader with dependence on gold bullion, exposing it to price volatility, supply constraints, forex, and import-duty risk; only 373 customers, a real concentration risk. Borrowings have risen to ₹111.11 Cr.
FY26 revenue grew 37.69% and PAT grew 158.23%, with ROE 56.45% and ROCE 52.08% - strong on paper, but IPO Central explicitly pairs this with a caution on thin margins and rising leverage.
~46% of the issue is an offer for sale, which 'will not benefit the company' per IPO Central - a large share of proceeds is going to sellers monetizing, not the business.

GMP discrepancy: independent trackers showed ₹42 / 23.73% (implied listing ₹219) at time of search, materially below the ~31% figure in our computed data - worth re-checking closer to listing since GMP moves hourly.
items.source: IPO Central, cross-check vs our data

items.text: Multiple trackers (Chanakya Nipothi, Chittorgarh) converge on a 'Selective Apply' framing conditioned on final subscription/QIB momentum, not an outright buy call.
No credible named anchor investor list surfaced in searches.

Deepa Jewellers Limited.adjustment_reason: Broadly consistent with the computed CONSIDER at 0.48 confidence - the low confidence is appropriate given thin margins, customer concentration, and heavy OFS. The lower independently-observed GMP (23.7% vs our 31%) argues against nudging this toward APPLY; re-check both figures once bidding opens.

Rays Of Belief Limited.summary: A compelling ROE/margin story funds an aggressive, execution-heavy expansion into a talent-constrained sector at a rich valuation alongside full promoter exit — a classic story-stock pattern the ratios alone don't flag, and one source directly contradicts our margin-expansion figures.

items.text: Business is a for-profit social enterprise (brand 'Mom's Belief') delivering intervention plans for children with neurodevelopmental disorders (autism, ADHD, Down syndrome, CP); 136 centres across 57 cities as of March 2026.
Proceeds are earmarked to open 319 new centres between FY27-FY29 - an aggressive, execution-dependent plan in a sector facing a 'systemic shortage of specialized clinical talent'.

DISCREPANCY: one source (Chanakya Nipothi via IPO Central) describes 'declining FY26 PAT', which conflicts with our computed margin-expansion figures (PAT margin 16.15%, up from 6.07%). This should be resolved against the actual RHP financials before trusting either figure at face value.
items.source: Chanakya Nipothi via IPO Central - conflicts with ipos.json

items.text: Post-issue P/E of 100.84x (market cap ₹499.55 Cr) is flagged industry-wide as rich, 'leaving little margin of safety'.

DATA NOTE: promoter_post=0.00% follows the same pattern as Priority Jewels, Purple Style Labs, and Complete Sports (0% OFS, likely an unfilled source placeholder rather than a confirmed full exit) - no independent source confirms a literal 100% exit.
GMP as of 26 Aug was ₹18 (7.53%), lower than the ~11.3% in our computed data but consistent with a premium that has been rising from 0% toward listing.

Rays Of Belief Limited.adjustment_reason: I would lean below the computed NEUTRAL toward caution for listing-gain seekers, not because of a clean reason to override the verdict, but because the unresolved PAT discrepancy plus a 100x P/E funding an execution-heavy expansion stack multiple soft-data red flags that the computed 0.78 confidence may be overstating. Resolve the PAT conflict against the RHP before the closing-day call.
